title: A typo in a dotted name shows as {key}, not as nothing
why: Interpolation has one job besides showing values: making a typo VISIBLE. An unset bare name renders as the literal `{key}` for exactly that reason — the author sees the braces and finds the mistake. A dotted name is the same kind of mistake and by far the likelier one: imported stats are namespaced (`Way.Moral`, `Relationships.Ivan`), so the author types two words instead of one and has two chances to slip. C# treated a dot as proof of an EXPRESSION and rendered nothing at all: the number vanished mid-sentence with no trace, and the author had no way to tell a wrong name from a wrong value. The browser player showed the braces. Two runtimes, one question, opposite answers — and the silent one was in the app the player actually runs. Пустое значение по пути показывается так же, как промах: отличить «пути нет» от «путь есть, значение пусто» не умеет ни один рантайм — оба спрашивают значение и получают «ничего». Раз отличить нельзя, ответ обязан быть один, и выбран полезный автору.
